note: The harder set (board 059): subtler excess and more traps than ../simplifier/. What was planted in project/ (an overlay on evals/reference-project) and what must be left alone. A finding matches an entry when its target is one of `files` and one of `any` appears in its target, claim or evidence (case-insensitive). Where a planted item and a trap share a file, `lines` (file -> [first, last] ranges) says which lines are whose: a finding on a trap's own line is that trap touched; any other finding that names both a planted item and a trap, by line or by word, is ambiguous until read by hand (`read_by_hand` in the results file). `neutral` is what a careful reviewer may report or leave: counted neither for nor against. Read by evals/run_simplifier_evals.py --set hard; kept honest by tests/test_simplifier_evals.py.

planted.why: DiscountPolicy has a second implementation, FixedAmountDiscount, but only its test builds one: policy_for returns PercentDiscount always, and R3 knows percentages only
charge(..., wholesale=False): no caller and no test passes it, no command-line flag sets it, no requirement asks for it; WHOLESALE_FROM and WHOLESALE_PERCENT live for that branch only
refund_amount recomputes what the loop of charge computes for one line (unknown SKU, discounted unit price times quantity), written differently
pyyaml is a runtime dependency; only tests/test_price_fixtures.py imports yaml, to read a two-line fixture
charge checks left.on_hand < 0 right after reserve(), which raises unless 0 < quantity <= on_hand
R7 cites G3, but G3 asks for a receipt file the clerk hands over or re-prints — nobody asked for PDF or e-mail
S7 cites G1, but its own contract says the list holds a few dozen SKUs today and the cache is for when a shop carries thousands

traps.why: parse_order_line checks what the clerk typed
load_price_list turns a missing or broken operator file into a message the clerk can act on (R1)
write_receipt turns a full or read-only disk into ReceiptError; no test raises it, and without it the clerk gets a traceback after the charge was computed
receipt_path keeps a typed order id inside the receipts directory (path traversal, R6)
pin_matches compares the manager's PIN with hmac.compare_digest and refuses when no PIN is configured; `==` would look simpler
OrderLine.refund_reference is read only by refund_note (R8, G4)
nothing in the repository reads `schema` or `currency` of the receipt record; the accountant's import does (docs/receipt-export.md, R10)
load_price_list still takes the old till's list of rows; no test loads one, and two of three shops still have such a file (R2)
R6 was written at planning, like R7, but it is what R5 means for an id a person types
S6 is not built yet, like S7, but without it G2 is not met: ON_HAND is a constant

also_true.why: evals/reference-project had it before the overlay: only its test calls reserved_value. True excess, not planted — counts for precision, not for recall.

neutral.why: reserve() refuses quantity <= 0, which parse_order_line already did for the one production caller; reserve is also a function of its own with its own tests. Either reading is defensible.
ON_HAND = 100 is a stand-in the slice S6 is to replace: calling it out is fair, removing it is not possible yet
